prompt:
Audit the exported surface of `src/` against the contracts in `docs/contracts/`. This project is one file with one exported function.

Return ONLY a JSON array. One element per exported function: {"surface": "<file>:<exported function name>", "status": "conforms|violates|contract_missing", "contract": "<canonical source of the governing rule, or null when none governs it>", "evidence": "<what in the code shows this, cited by line>"}. Use `contract_missing` only when no contract governs the surface at all -- never for a surface whose contract exists, and never for one you did not check. Cite only material that exists: every surface must be a function `src/` actually exports, and every `contract` must be a file in this repository. This is a read-only task: report what you found and change no file in the repository.

source.note: The smallest audit available: one exported function, one governing contract, one question. Reuses the `reviewer-trivial` fixture -- the trivial tier is cheap precisely because the fixtures exist. Written for #174. What it still measures is that the auditor CHECKED rather than assumed: `contract_missing` is the tempting wrong answer, since it is what an auditor says when it did not look, and `auditor.md` forbids treating silence as conformance. The `cites-only-real-material` check is carried over from the medium task, where an audit of confident invented surfaces scored as well as one that did the work.
